A1.evidence: The paper's own analysis scripts (principal code artefact under the aggregation rule) are retrievable by DOI over HTTPS: pack http_status 200, access_right 'open'. The data-completeness override applies to data only.

A1_1.evidence: DOI resolution plus HTTPS download from Zenodo - open, free, universally implementable protocol; no registration, subscription, or proprietary client needed (pack resolved both records unauthenticated with HTTP 200).

A1_2.evidence: Fully open software deposit (access_right 'open') requiring no authentication; under v2.1 this satisfies A1.2 (the protocol supports authentication where needed, and none is needed). No warranted-but-undocumented access control exists.

A2.evidence: Zenodo Row 2 entitlements: metadata always publicly accessible, tombstone page with DOI and URL retained on withdrawal, records preserved for the lifetime of the repository; a live DataCite metadata record for the software is confirmed in the pack. The code is not GitHub-only - the paper itself notes GitHub 'does not offer DOIs or the same commitments to long-term availability as Zenodo' (p. 7).

F1.evidence: "The entire R code (R Core Team, 2024) used for all the analysis and visualizations contained in this paper is at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252" (p. 2) - the software has its own Zenodo DOI; pack confirms DataCite resource_type 'Software' and Zenodo resource_type 'software'.

F2.evidence: Structured DataCite/Zenodo metadata for the software record: metadata_record true, publisher 'Zenodo', publication_year 2025, resource_type 'Software', state 'findable', and the descriptive title 'benmarwick/web-of-science-archaeology: Research compendium for the publication "Is archaeology a science?"' recorded in the pack.

F3.evidence: Pack field identifier_in_metadata: true for the software record at both DataCite and Zenodo; the record additionally carries concept_doi 10.5281/zenodo.14897252 alongside version doi 10.5281/zenodo.15603267.

F4.evidence: Software record indexed in searchable registries: resolvable at the DataCite API with state 'findable' and returned as the top hit by the Zenodo search query recorded in the pack's recovery block.

I1.evidence: Analysis is plain-text R source code in an open, broadly applicable language: "The entire R code (R Core Team, 2024) used for all the analysis and visualizations contained in this paper" (p. 2); no compiled binaries or proprietary-only formats are described.

I2.evidence: Looked for CodeMeta, schema.org software metadata, or other FAIR vocabulary use in the software deposit. The pack's fields for the software record list no vocabulary or subject scheme, the paper names none, and no listed platform entitlement supplies one (Zenodo Row 2 guarantees DataCite metadata only).

I3.evidence: Looked for qualified, PID-typed references from the software record to other resources (article DOI via isSupplementTo, dependency PIDs). The pack records no relatedIdentifiers for either the DataCite or Zenodo software record; under the aggregation rule third-party dependencies enter only through citation quality, and no PID-typed dependency references are evidenced at artefact level.

R1.evidence: Code described with a plurality of relevant attributes: language and version source (R Core Team, 2024), scope ("all the analysis and visualizations contained in this paper"), reproduction claim ("All the figures, tables, and statistical test results presented here can be independently reproduced with the code and data in this compendium"), organisation as a research compendium citing Marwick et al. (2018), and supplementary model-specification/diagnostic documentation deposited at the same DOI (Fig. 2 caption).

R1_1.evidence: Licence identified: "The R code is released under the MIT license" (p. 2); the service records cc-by-4.0 for the same deposit and the pack flags the same-artefact disagreement, so the more restrictive CC-BY-4.0 governs scoring. A named, machine-readable licence is present under either reading (not a bare mandatory field).

R1_2.evidence: Provenance documented: authorship and deposit date in the DataCite record (publication_year 2025, publisher Zenodo), version lineage evidenced by concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14897252 resolving to versioned record 10.5281/zenodo.15603267 (GitHub-linked release of benmarwick/web-of-science-archaeology), R environment cited (R Core Team, 2024), and the data sources and processing steps the code consumes described in Methods (p. 2).

R1_3.evidence: Code-side qualifying standard met: the analysis is packaged as a research compendium following the documented compendium/package structure of Marwick et al. (2018) ("the code and data in this compendium (Marwick et al., 2018)", p. 2; the deposit title is 'Research compendium for the publication "Is archaeology a science?"'), and the deposit additionally carries a DataCite metadata record (route (a)). Methodological standards were not counted.

barriers: Peer-review confidentiality: the 25 manuscripts submitted to JAS that were reproducibility-reviewed (Section 5, Fig. 5) are unpublished submissions and are not retrievable (Tier 3); only the author's coded summary of their characteristics is reproducible from the compendium.

Subscription paywall: the upstream Clarivate Web of Science search (Archaeology category, document type 'article', n = 28,871) and the Journal Citation Indicator h-index rankings used to select the 20 journals require institutional licence access (Tier 2, accessible with manual steps).

Link-resolution note (does not affect the principal artefact): the evidence pack records a second declared Zenodo identifier, 10.5281/zenodo.14561925, as unresolved (HTTP 404) at both DataCite and Zenodo, with bounded recovery pointing to the compendium's versioned record 10.5281/zenodo.15603267; the compendium DOI cited in the Methods and data availability statement (10.5281/zenodo.14897252) resolves normally.

A1.evidence: Retrievable by DOI over HTTPS (pack http_status 200, access_right 'open'), and data_completeness coverage_category is 'substantial' (4 of 5 enumerated datasets at Tier 0-2), so the completeness override does not trigger. The paper states all figures, tables, and statistical test results are reproducible from the code and data in the compendium (p. 2).

A1_1.evidence: Access is via DOI resolution and HTTPS to Zenodo - open, free, universally implementable; pack shows access_right 'open' and HTTP 200 on the public Zenodo and DataCite APIs with no authentication.

A1_2.evidence: Fully open resource requiring no authentication (access_right 'open'); under instrument v2.1 the protocol supports authentication where needed and none is needed here. No access control exists or is warranted (bibliometric records and review-coding summaries; no human-subject or Indigenous data).

A2.evidence: Deposit is on Zenodo, whose Row 2 entitlements include a tombstone page on withdrawal with DOI and URL retained and metadata always publicly accessible; the pack confirms a live DataCite metadata record carrying the identifier.

F1.evidence: Data deposited under its own Zenodo DOI: "The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252" (p. 10). Evidence pack confirms the DOI resolves at DataCite with state 'findable' and at Zenodo (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14897252, version 10.5281/zenodo.15603267).

F2.evidence: Pack records metadata_record: true with substantive DataCite values - publisher 'Zenodo', publication_year 2025, resource_type 'Software', state 'findable', and a descriptive title recorded in the pack's recovery block ('benmarwick/web-of-science-archaeology: Research compendium for the publication "Is archaeology a science?"'); Zenodo Row 2 guarantees DataCite metadata. Values are substantive, not null-codes (Row 1 caveat checked).

F3.evidence: Pack field identifier_in_metadata: true for both the DataCite and Zenodo records of the deposit (doi 10.5281/zenodo.14897252; version doi 10.5281/zenodo.15603267 with concept_doi recorded in-record).

F4.evidence: Record is indexed and retrievable in searchable registries: resolved via the DataCite REST API (state 'findable') and returned by a Zenodo full-text search query recorded in the pack's recovery block. Zenodo/DataCite indexing is also a listed Row 2 entitlement.

I1.evidence: The data are machine-actionable inputs to executable R code: "All the figures, tables, and statistical test results presented here can be independently reproduced with the code and data in this compendium (Marwick et al., 2018)" (p. 2) - i.e. structured, script-parseable data files rather than PDF/Word tables. No PDF- or image-only data distribution is described anywhere in the paper.

I2.evidence: Looked for controlled vocabularies, ontologies, or PID-bearing term schemes for the bibliometric variables (number of authors, relative title length, page count, recency and diversity of references) and for the Fig. 5 review-coding categories (GMM, AI/ML, MCMC, 'Incomplete', 'Dependencies', 'Path'). The paper names no vocabulary standard and the pack records no subject/vocabulary scheme; coding categories are ad hoc field names.

I3.evidence: Looked for typed/qualified references (relatedIdentifiers such as isSupplementTo the article DOI, or PID-typed links to the Web of Science source) in the deposit metadata. The pack's fields for both the DataCite and Zenodo records list no relatedIdentifiers (only doi, licences, publisher, resource_type, state, concept_doi), and no listed platform entitlement supplies them.

R1.evidence: Data described with a plurality of relevant attributes: source database and query ("Clarivate's Web of Science database by first selecting the Web of Science category 'Archaeology' and the Document type 'article' (n = 28,871)"), filtering rules (top-ranking 25 journals by h-index; journals with fewer than 100 articles excluded, resulting in 20 journals), sample and date range (9697 papers, 1975-2025), five defined bibliometric variables, plus deposit-level title, creator, publisher, year, and type in the Zenodo/DataCite record.

R1_1.evidence: Licence identified, not merely a populated field. Paper asserts "the data as CC-0" (p. 2); the hosting service records cc-by-4.0 for the same deposit and the pack flags this as a same-artefact disagreement. Applying the most-restrictive rule (v2.1 R1.1 case (b)), CC-BY-4.0 governs - a clear, accessible, machine-readable licence either way.

R1_2.evidence: Detailed provenance: creation process documented (Web of Science extraction, category/document-type/h-index filtering), software environment named (R Core Team, 2024), model specifications and diagnostics deposited alongside (Fig. 2 caption), and versioned deposit history evidenced by concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14897252 resolving to version 10.5281/zenodo.15603267.

R1_3.evidence: Deposit-level standard met via qualifying route (a): the Zenodo deposit carries a DataCite metadata record (pack metadata_record: true, identifier_in_metadata: true; Row 2 entitlement) with substantive creator/title/publisher/year/resource-type values. Methodological practices described in the paper were not counted towards R1.3.
